newsitem.title: USA: Higher-yielding emerging market debt rises sharply.
newsitem.headline: Higher-yielding emerging market debt rises sharply.

text.p: Emerging market debt posted strong gains on Thursday after key U.S. economic data sparked a U.S. Treasury market rally, traders and analysts said.
Bulgaria discounts BGFLTH24A=RR shot up two percentage points to 71-1/4 bid, tightening about 55 basis points to comparable Treasuries.

"I don't know that there's anything definite in the fundamental news today. There's just somebody out there buying Bulgaria bonds," said Dan Peirce, chief emerging markets strategist at Bank of Boston.
An environment of rising ratings and declining risk has pushed some investors into formerly fringe countries, Peirce said.
"It may be only 600 or 700 (basis points) over, but Bulgaria is about as dicey as you can get," he said.

Funds flowed into Russian debt as well, thanks to favorable market talk on the country's forthcoming Eurobond, traders said. Dollar-denominated Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were up 7/8 at 90-1/4, and MinFins were up between 1/4 and 5/8.
"They've got a 10-year Eurobond that's supposed to come out at 350 or 375 (basis points) over," well below spreads for existing 10-year Russia debt, one trader explained.
Ecuador bonds tightened between 20 and 45 basis points the day after President Fabian Alarcon unveiled a package of mild fiscal measures.

Alarcon said Ecuador would trim profit margins of gasoline businesses, raise state revenues and cut electricity subsidies. But investors' thirst for yield drove Ecuador bonds' performance far more than the widely anticipated fiscal measures, traders said.
In late trading, Ecuador discounts ECDISC=RR were up 1-1/4 at 74 bid and PDIs ECPDI=RR were up one point at 67-7/8 bid.
Major Latin America issues rose in step with Treasuries. Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were up 7/8 at 80-5/8, and Argentina FRBs ARFLC05 had risen 3/8 to 94-1/4.
A weak reading on U.S. retail sales for May evidenced a slowing of domestic consumer demand and prompted a full-point rise in the price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond, U.S. analysts said.
Late on Thursday, the long bond was up 30/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
